_description: Living log of in-progress tasks, architectural decisions, known bugs, and ongoing migrations. Updated via the log-task tool.

decisions.title: Landlord onboarding nudge: daily cron + 24h non-overlapping window
decisions.description: Added a once-daily Vercel Cron (15:00 UTC) hitting /api/cron/landlord-nudge that emails landlords who signed up in the last 24h but have no listings. Chose an exact 24h lookback with no dedup column: a fixed daily run + 24h window tiles signups into non-overlapping windows, so each landlord is caught exactly once (no schema change needed). Accepted edge case: a fully failed run skips that day's cohort. Email copy is the warm 'Having trouble?' variant with reply-to info@useproximity.org as a support channel.
decisions.context: PR #59 into staging (feat/landlord-nudge-email). Files: vercel.json, src/app/api/cron/landlord-nudge/route.js, src/lib/email.js (sendLandlordNudgeEmail). Requires CRON_SECRET env var set in Vercel before it runs in prod.

decisions.title: Matchmaking algorithm: budget-window + priority-met-at-budget headline + saturation spread
decisions.description: How the proxy-chat matchmaking system works (feat/proxy-chat). PIPELINE: (1) Fixed deterministic question script (questionScript.js QUESTION_PLAN) -> answers become numeric `weights` over 9 dims via WEIGHT_MAP/PRIORITY_WEIGHTS + RANK_BUMPS (steep [1.0,0.5,0.3...] so #1 priority dominates). recomputeFromPreferences (questionEngine.js) re-derives weights identically from a completed prefs object. (2) chatOrchestrator.computeRecommendations -> listingFilter.rankListings. (3) rankListings: buildRankContext builds a DIVERSE pool (spanning price/reviews/proximity/amenities) and computes a deterministic per-listing fit score (computeFitScores) over data dims; Haiku (claude-haiku-4-5, PROXY_CHAT_KEY) ranks lower slots. THE TOP 3 ARE DETERMINISTIC (selectTopThree), not LLM: #1 = the most-EXPENSIVE IN-BUDGET listing that satisfies the student's #1 stated priority (we give them what they asked for at their budget, not what's 'objectively best'); #2/#3 = spinoffs on the SAME priority each leading a different plus (value/amenities/reviews/proximity). KEY POLICIES: budget is a hard WINDOW, not a cheaper-is-better gradient (the `budget` weight dim is excluded from fit; within budget all prices are equal). 'value' = bang-for-buck (quality per $), not absolute cheapness. Proximity is split into campus/med_campus/grocery via proximity_targets (med-year auto-seeds med_campus; free text parsed by REFINE_SYSTEM). Blank listing titles fall back to street address. SATURATION (new): fetchSaturation reads the live DB demand signal (user_listing_interactions 'contacted' = weight 2, prior matchmaking_chat_sessions.recommendations = weight 1) and uses it as a TIE-BREAKER ONLY among near-equal candidates in selectTopThree, so oversubscribed listings get edged out and demand spreads (never overrides priority or busts budget).
decisions.context: Files: src/lib/matchmaking/{listingFilter,questionEngine,chatOrchestrator,questionScript}.js, listing-filter.skill.md. Test harnesses (dev-only, reusable): /api/dev/matchmaking-probe + scripts/matchmaking-probe.mjs (bias/concentration); /api/dev/matchmaking-saturation-sim + scripts/matchmaking-saturation-sim.mjs (control vs saturation spread, in-memory). Sim result (150 students): distinct #1 picks 18->30, busiest-listing share 28%->15%, HHI 0.128->0.069, with a FLAT timeline (no penalty to early users). Open follow-ups: optional saturation decay window so filled listings aren't penalized forever; ability to turn saturation strength up past tie-break-only. Not yet pushed; branch feat/proxy-chat.

decisions.title: MCP knowledge is committed to git (shared across machines and agents)
decisions.description: mcp/knowledge/ is no longer gitignored (except agent-sessions.json, a machine-local runtime log). Every clone now ships the same repo knowledge, so any contributor's coding agent understands the repo and others' changes without running the MCP first. generate-knowledge.mjs is idempotent (skips rewrites when only the _generated timestamp would change), so regeneration is diff-clean. A CI workflow (.github/workflows/update-knowledge.yml) regenerates and auto-commits drift after pushes to staging/main that touch apps/web/src — this covers contributors who never run the MCP locally. Convention: regenerate and commit knowledge together with code changes; db-schema.json remains hand-maintained against the live DB.
decisions.context: Branch feat/shared-mcp-knowledge; also updated CLAUDE.md, .gitignore, release-pr-check.yml comment, and domain.json workflow.knowledgeMaintenance text.

decisions.title: Matchmaking excludes subleases by default; sublease ≠ sublease_friendly
decisions.description: Proxy matchmaking now excludes sublease listings by default: applySubleasePref (listingFilter.js) drops any listing whose active unit_leases are ALL sublease rows (priced or not — unpriced sublease posts previously slipped through via the room-data path) unless preferences.exclude_subleases === false, which the chat agent sets only when the student explicitly asks for subleases. New exported predicate isSubleaseListing() is the single source of truth; slimCandidate exposes is_sublease to the ranking model and market catalog, and shownListingsContext exposes isSublease to the chat agent. Key semantics: unit_leases.sublease = the lease IS a sublease; listings.sublease_friendly = subletting is ALLOWED (the agent previously conflated these). Also fixed: tradeoff "No strong preference" chip rendered the raw __unsure__ sentinel in the user's bubble (answerToLabel checked kind before the UNSURE sentinel). Data fix: 6038 Westminster Place's active lease was mislabeled sublease=false — corrected in dev; SAME FIX STILL PENDING IN PROD (one-row UPDATE, awaiting approval).
decisions.context: Branch feat/proxy-chat. Files: apps/web/src/lib/matchmaking/{listingFilter.js,chatOrchestrator.js,questionEngine.js,listing-filter.skill.md}. Verified via scratchpad harness against dev DB: 10 subleases in universe, 0 in default search, all flagged is_sublease=true on opt-in.

decisions.title: Matchmaking: description is primary evidence; re-ranks never repeat shown listings
decisions.description: Two ranking-policy changes on feat/proxy-chat. (1) Listing descriptions are now a heavily-weighted, near-authoritative ranking signal: the listing-filter skill + runtime instruction tell the ranker to boost candidates whose description confirms a stated preference/note, demote on conflicts, rule out hard conflicts, and trust the description over structured fields when they disagree; the excerpt passed to the model widened from 320 to 600 chars. (2) Never-repeat re-ranks: any re-rank after recommendations exist (agent update_search, preference-panel PATCH in route.js, rewound answer edits) folds currently shown listing ids into preferences._setAside first, so refines always return entirely new cards. The old "smart repeats" behavior (preference changes cleared _setAside) is removed. Fallbacks: update_search restores previous cards with an honest note when nothing new fits (distinguishing "seen everything that fits" vs "nothing fits at all" via filterEligible without set-aside); finalizeRecommendations clears _setAside and retries rather than going empty on rewound flows; PATCH rolls back the set-aside when it can't produce fresh picks. update_search tool result now includes previous_top {title, still_best_overall} computed by deterministic fit comparison (buildRankContext over the unrestricted pool) so the agent can truthfully say the old #1 is still the best overall fit.
decisions.context: Files: apps/web/src/lib/matchmaking/{chatOrchestrator.js,listingFilter.js,listing-filter.skill.md}, apps/web/src/app/api/matchmaking/chat/route.js. Verified against dev DB: back-to-back re-rank returned 3/3 new listings, zero overlap; previous_top fit comparison behaves honestly.

decisions.title: Auto-unavailable: hourly auto-hide of landlord-reported-leased listings + change-driven review email
decisions.description: Landlord "leased" reports from the email check-in system (proximity-automation repo) are now acted on automatically: an hourly cron (/api/cron/auto-unavailable) hides still-visible reported listings via the audited rpc_pms_apply (whole listing for single-unit reports; only the reported bedroom types' listing_units for multi-unit), verifies each hide against the public /api/listings immediately, records before/after in the new auto_unavailable_actions table (migration applied to dev AND prod), and emails a review digest (AUTO_UNAVAILABLE_ALERT_EMAIL or supers) with one-click signed Undo links — only on runs where something changed. Key policies: detection mirrors the site's effective-visibility rule (matches the leasing dashboard's "Remove from site" panel exactly); each report is actioned at most once (fingerprint listing_id + last_verified_at) so undos/manual relists are never fought; landlord corrections surface in the email but never auto-relist; NEVER deletes, NEVER writes check-in columns (checkin_*, last_verified_*, unit_type_status, etc. are read-only signal), NEVER emails landlords; skips PMS-connected, deleted, and TEST- rows (?include_test=1 for rehearsals; ?dry_run=1 / AUTO_UNAVAILABLE_DRY_RUN=1 computes without writing). Undo links: HMAC (AVAILABILITY_LINK_SECRET||AUTH_SECRET), 14-day expiry, single-use via action-row status, scanner-safe two-step GET→POST. Phase-0 finding recorded for posterity: there is NO MongoDB — /api/listings reads prod Supabase directly; the 2026-07-10 "Postgres writes don't control the site" conclusion was wrong (proven empirically on a synthetic prod listing with full-row diffs + audit log).
decisions.context: PR #137 (feat/auto-unavailable → staging), worktree ../Proximity-auto-unavailable. Files: apps/web/src/lib/autoUnavailable.js, apps/web/src/app/api/cron/auto-unavailable/route.js, apps/web/src/app/api/auto-unavailable/undo/route.js, supabase/migrations/20260808_auto_unavailable_actions.sql, vercel.json (hourly cron; needs Vercel Pro), outreach.js (new OUTREACH_TEST_RECIPIENT for cron-context test emails). Ben's decisions 2026-08-08: apply-immediately + review-after (supersedes the handoff plan's approve-first), no dry-run day, hourly cadence, automation repo remains sole landlord check-in sender. On prod deploy: 6 outstanding leased listings hidden within the first hour. Cross-repo follow-ups: automation repo should exclude pms_connection_id listings from check-ins; last_verified_* becomes co-written once PR #116 ships.

findings.title: Listing-draft render chain: Firecrawl strips the site nav (onlyMainContent), Jina is out of credit, and a markdown-only render can win the length score
findings.description:
Measured 2026-09-15 against https://www.macapartments.com/ (Cloudflare Turnstile, so the plain fetch is a 403 "blocked" and the render chain always runs). IMPORTANT: staging and main run RENDER_FALLBACKS = [Firecrawl, Jina, Tavily] and stop at the first render clearing 800 characters, so PRODUCTION uses Firecrawl. The Jina-first reordering with looksPriced() lives only on the unpushed feat/listing-source-sync branch; points 2 and 3 below bite there, point 1 bites everywhere.

1. FIRECRAWL STRIPS THE NAV (the production bug). renderPageViaFirecrawl posted {url, formats:['html'], timeout} and never set onlyMainContent:false, so Firecrawl's default main-content extraction removed header/nav/footer. Its 34,432 bytes of HTML carried 33 anchors, none of them site nav: /searchlisting and the Chicago / St. Louis / Kansas City links were gone, extractLinks() returned 2 same-site links (both Kansas City properties), and the model's CANDIDATE LINKS had nothing to offer as an area folder. Setting onlyMainContent:false took the same page to 59,670 bytes and 12 internal + 16 external links including 'Search Apartments'.

2. JINA IS OUT OF CREDIT. r.jina.ai returns HTTP 402 InsufficientBalanceError (345-byte JSON body) for every URL with the key in apps/web/.env.local. renderPageViaJina catches !res.ok and returns null, so it fails silently. On the branch that puts Jina first, the 'free first link' therefore does nothing and every render pays Tavily and/or Firecrawl. Top it up or drop it from the chain.

3. A MARKDOWN-ONLY RENDER CAN WIN THE LENGTH SCORE. fetchPageSmart picks the render with the most htmlToText() characters. On the Mac homepage Tavily = 4,703 chars of text / 0 anchors, Firecrawl = 1,638 chars / 33 anchors, so Tavily won and extractLinks() returned ZERO. renderPageViaTavily wraps raw_content markdown in <html><body><div> with no <a> tags at all, so scoring on stripped-text length systematically prefers the source with the least structure. Fixed by keeping the best-text render for text and the most-anchored render for links and images (withLinkHtml / page.linkHtml).

Measured extraction cost on this site: $0.04 for the homepage, $0.33 for the 124-property /searchlisting page.

findings.title: Mac Properties site shape: 124 properties across 3 cities, only 13 in St. Louis; homepage carries an 8-item featured carousel
findings.description:
Mapped 2026-09-15 (firecrawl map, 193 URLs). macapartments.com is a RentCafe corporate site behind Cloudflare.

- Homepage = marketing page with a "Featured Properties" carousel of exactly 8 buildings (5252, Shoreland, Solstice on the Park, One Hundred Above the Park, Dorchester, Six40, International, Senate at The Crosswalks). That is the whole reason a paste of the root URL yields 8 properties: the import was faithful, the page only has 8.
- Real inventory is /searchlisting, which says "Showing 25 out of 124 properties." — paginated at 25.
- Per-city filter: /searchlisting?citystate=st.%20louis,mo returns all 13 St. Louis properties on one page (under the 25 cap, so no pagination needed). Pasting THAT url into the assisted importer works today and returns all 13 with correct addresses and same-site /apartments/mo/st.-louis/<slug>/default.aspx URLs. This is the working manual workaround.
- Property split by city: 101 Chicago, 38 Kansas City, 12-13 St. Louis (+1 stray NJ).
- The "Chicago / St. Louis / Kansas City" nav links go to rent.macapartments.com/<city>, which are HubSpot MARKETING pages, not property lists. They only contain a "View Available Apartments" button back to www.macapartments.com/searchlisting. Do not treat them as area folders.
- Several featured properties have their own domains (5252apartments.com, shorelandchicago.com, solsticechicago.com, liveat100.com, dorchesterapartments.com, senate-crosswalkskc.com). sameSite() rejects these, so targetProperty.url is nulled and picking one of them re-reads the corporate homepage instead of the property's own site.
- /sitemap.xml is Cloudflare-challenged (403). robots.txt is permissive but lists no sitemap.
findings.context: Relevant to the assisted add-listing importer and to landlord lead-gen. Mac is about to list a batch of St. Louis properties.

findings.title: Listing-import picker: what real landlord sites do to the near/far and identity rules
findings.description:
Measured 2026-09-15 by driving the real flow in Chromium (Playwright 1.62.1 from ~/course-runner) plus server-side extraction runs. Five site behaviours that any future change to the picker has to keep working.

1. A SITE CAN GIVE MANY BUILDINGS ONE NAME. altusproperties.com labels NINE different buildings "Pearl Street" on its homepage (1738 Pearl, 1701 Pearl, 1434 Spruce, ...), each with its own /properties/ path. Keying identity on the name alone collapsed all nine into one row. Keying on the URL alone re-broke Mac, which lists One Hundred Above the Park on its homepage as liveat100.com and again inside its St. Louis page as bare prose with no link. Working rule: same URL = same building; same NAME = same building unless both URLs sit on the same HOST (same host + different paths = a site really distinguishing two things it gave one label).

2. THE EXTRACTION DOES NOT ALWAYS RETURN A CITY. byroncompany.com owns 16 buildings, all in St. Louis. On one run every property came back with an address including "St. Louis"; on the next run the same page returned names only. Treating "not matched as near campus" as "far away" folded 14 of their 16 buildings into a collapsed disclosure. Rule that holds: only set a property aside when the page POSITIVELY places it elsewhere (a mailing address with a non-63xxx zip, or a city we can name). Unplaced means ours. Costs one extra ticked row on Mac (River Terrace Gardens), which is one untick.

3. A CITY MARKETING PAGE IS NOT AN INVENTORY. rent.macapartments.com/st-louis names 9 buildings in prose; macapartments.com/searchlisting?citystate=st.%20louis,mo holds the real 13. Merging both gives 14, because the marketing prose also yields a "Terrace" that appears nowhere in the inventory and is almost certainly "private terrace". Read the inventory page and leave the city pages for browsing.

4. REACT DOUBLE-INVOKES STATE UPDATERS IN DEV. The absorb pass built its result by pushing into an array from inside setTree(prev => ...). Dev ran it twice: 216 rows for a 124-property site and duplicate-key warnings. Compute merges outside the updater (a ref mirroring the tree works).

5. FIRECRAWL RATE-LIMITS UNDER A BATCH. Running 5 sites back to back made apartments.com fail with DraftFetchError "blocked", which surfaces to the landlord as "your website's security settings blocked our reader". The same URL alone succeeds in 36s. All three renderers failing soft to null is indistinguishable from a real block; a retry would help. onlyMainContent:false does NOT break apartments.com (199KB vs 141KB of HTML).

Regression set that passes (root paste, one extraction each, ~$0.05-0.33): macapartments.com (124 props, 13-14 near), byroncompany.com/apartments (16, all ticked), altusproperties.com (9 distinct Pearl Streets), clocktowercompany.com/collections/apartments (9 + inventory folder), demunrent.com, mckenziestl.com/floor-plans, ars.wustl.edu property page, mosaic314.com (Wix), terra-stl.com/floorplans (RentCafe, 5 floor plans / 53 units), apartments.com listing (Akamai, needs Firecrawl), zillow.com/b/ building page (5 units with numbers and rents).

Dev-flow note: the staging email-recipient modal blocks every click in an automated browser. Pre-set cookie staging_email_to to get past it. Login needs ~1.2s after networkidle before fill() sticks, or React has not hydrated and the form submits empty.

findings.title: RealPage/SightMap sites publish full unit pricing and lease terms via a public API; the page itself carries almost nothing
findings.description:
Measured 2026-09-15 on https://www.metroflatsstl.com (Metropolitan Flats, G5 marketing site over RealPage).

THE PAGE IS A DEAD END. The floor-plans page fetched normally is 32KB and never mentions the availability widget. Fully rendered it is 722KB and still contains only FOUR dollar figures and two unit numbers, for a building with 23 available apartments: the SightMap widget draws into a canvas and fetches its data afterwards. No amount of better scraping or a longer wait fixes this.

THE WIDGET'S API HAS EVERYTHING, PUBLIC AND UNAUTHENTICATED. Four steps:
  1. Render the page with Firecrawl waitFor:9000 (the plain render will NOT do) and read the embed token out of https://sightmap.com/embed/<embedToken>. For Metro Flats: 9zw47600w87.
  2. GET https://sightmap.com/embed/<embedToken> as plain HTML (no JS needed). It names its own API path: api/v1/<apiToken>/sightmaps/<id>, e.g. api/v1/1ywy7dzowq0/sightmaps/65968. The embed token and the API token are DIFFERENT strings; do not assume one from the other.
  3. GET https://sightmap.com/app/api/v1/<apiToken>/sightmaps/<id> (75KB JSON). data.units[] gives unit_number, price, area, available_on, display_available_on, display_lease_term, floor_plan_id, specials_description, plus a per-unit leasing_price_url. data.floor_plans[] gives name, bedroom_count, bathroom_count, image_url.
  4. GET a unit's leasing_price_url for the WHOLE LEASE-TERM MATRIX, e.g. Newstead: 7mo $2203, 8mo $2091, 9mo $2019, 10mo $2019, 11mo $2333, 12mo $2036, 13mo $2135, 14mo $1974, 15mo $1978. The apply_url in each option confirms RealPage (9200076.onlineleasing.realpage.com). Fetch this ONCE PER FLOOR PLAN, not per unit: which terms a building offers does not vary unit to unit, and Metro Flats would otherwise be 23 requests to learn one list.

TRIGGER: the string "realpage" appears 5 times in the UN-rendered HTML even though "sightmap" appears zero times. That is what gates the expensive waited render, so ordinary landlord sites never pay for it. Verified demunrent.com does not trigger it.

RESULT: Metro Flats now imports as 5 floor plans (Newstead, Pershing, Taylor, Maryland, Euclid) with real unit numbers per plan, whole-unit prices, availability dates and leaseTermMonths [7,8,9,10,11,12,13,14,15]. Extraction cost $0.11.

OTHER FEEDS ON THE SAME PAGE, not used but live if ever needed: doorway-api.knockrentals.com/v1/property/<id>/units (Knock, 23 units with price/availableOn/bedrooms/bathrooms/layoutName, no lease terms) and .../property/community/<hash>. Knock's property id for Metro Flats is 2031106.
